name: check_brand
title: Check the brand
description: Runs blazon check on the brand, without plugins, and returns its findings and counts. Plugins in blazon.json do not run, so the counts can be lower than `blazon check` prints, but only for a plugin with a check role; a build-only plugin adds no finding. `pluginsSkipped` and `warnings` list every configured plugin, since a role is known only by starting the plugin; `rulesNotRun` gives the code pattern of each (`name/*`). `byRule` groups the findings by code with a count and one example each. `passed` is false when the brand's own data has errors (`brandHasErrors`), and values read from such a brand can be wrong; a `pin-mismatch` finding is listed and counted but does not make `passed` false, and is also in `pinMismatch`. Returns at most `limit` findings (default 50, at most 500); `counts` stay whole. Not for reading a value: use get_token.

severity.description: List only the findings at this level or worse. The counts stay whole

limit.description: The most findings to return, from 1 to 500; default 50

warnings.description: Lines blazon printed on standard error, such as a warning that the brand has errors. Empty when blazon said nothing

brandHasErrors.description: True when the brand's own data has error findings, so a value read from it may be wrong. Run check_brand to see them. A blazon.lock that names another blazon build does not set it: that is `pinMismatch`

pinned.description: The blazon build blazon.lock names, as blazon prints it (12 hex digits)

running.description: The blazon build running, as blazon prints it, or "unknown" when it cannot say

message.description: One line: which build the book is pinned to, which is running, and what to do

pinMismatch.description: Present only when blazon.lock names a different blazon build than the one running. The build and the book disagree; no token or value is wrong because of it, so there is no need to re-check values. Tell the user. `blazon check`, `build` and `tokens` refuse until it is fixed

truncated.description: True when the answer was cut to fit the size limit. `notice` says how to narrow the question

notice.description: Present when the answer was cut: how much was kept and how to ask a narrower question

passed.description: True when no finding other than the pin family is an error. A pin-mismatch alone leaves it true

errors.description: How many findings are errors, whatever `severity` or `limit` asked for

counts.description: How many findings the brand has at each level

code.description: The finding code, such as starter-logo-unchanged

findingsTotal.description: How many findings there are before `limit` cut the list

count.description: How many findings carry this code at this severity, before `limit` cut the list

example.description: The first finding of this code

path.description: Where the first finding of this code is, cut to 80 characters

message.description: What it says, cut to 120 characters

byRule.description: The findings grouped by code, worst severity first, then the larger count: what the warnings are without reading the list. Counted over every finding the check returned, not only the `limit` kept; with `severity` set, only that level and worse

rulesNotRun.description: The code pattern of each plugin that did not run, such as `blazon.copy/*`. A plugin finding code starts with its name and a slash, so no code matching one of these is in `findings`, and its absence says nothing about the brand. Absent when the config lists no plugin

pluginsSkipped.description: Every plugin blazon.json lists, which did not run because the server never starts a plugin. Only one with a check role can make `blazon check` report more findings than `counts`; the server cannot tell which without starting it. Absent when the config lists none

name: list_tokens
title: List the tokens
description: Lists the design tokens of the brand, or of one group, type or tier, each with its path, type, tier and value, in the order the token files write them. Use it to find a path or to read many values at once. `tier` (primitive, semantic or component) keeps to one layer of the brand. `theme` gives the values as that theme resolves them, and `defaultValue` on a token the theme changes; `themes` names the themes the brand has. For a token's CSS variable names and rules use get_token; for the brand's usage rules use get_rules. An answer over 40000 characters is cut to whole tokens, and `tokensTotal` says how many matched: narrow with `group`, `type` or `tier`.

group.description: A group path as list_tokens returns it, the part of a token path before its last dot (a path of the form `<group>.<token>` has the group `<group>`). Leave out for every token. Run list_tokens first to see the brand's groups

type.description: A token type, for example color, dimension or fontFamily. Leave out for every type. An unknown type is refused with the list of types

tier.description: A tier: primitive, semantic or component. Leave out for every tier. An unknown tier is refused with the list of tiers

theme.description: List the values in this context of the resolver's theme modifier, such as dark. An unknown theme is refused with the list of themes. Default: the default tokens

warnings.description: Lines blazon printed on standard error, such as a warning that the brand has errors. Empty when blazon said nothing

The build and the book disagree; no token or value is wrong because of it, so there is no need to re-check values. Tell the user. `blazon check`, `build` and `tokens` refuse until it is fixed

name: can_use
title: Can this color be used here
description: Answers whether one color token may be text on another color token, by the brand rules. Give `fg` and `bg` for one pair, or `pairs` (at most 50) for several in one call: the answer then has one result per pair, in order, and `allowed` is true only when every pair is. Exactly one of the two forms. Set `role` to ui for a focus ring, border or icon stroke: it is judged against the 3:1 non-text contrast and the pairs rules do not apply. `verbose` false leaves out the `checks` of an allowed answer; a denial keeps them. Contrast is measured as `check_brand` measures it: a color with an alpha channel is blended over its background, and `alpha` sets the foreground's opacity. The usage rules are read first, so a token a rule forbids is a denial even when it is not a color. A background with an alpha channel is an error, because what is behind it is not known, and so is a token that is not a color when usage allows it. A denied answer is a normal result (`allowed` is false, `reason` names the rule), not an error. Pairs come only from the `pairs` rules of token groups; component tokens are not read for them. For a color you have not picked, find one with list_tokens and type color.

fg.description: The text color token path, as list_tokens returns it for a color token. Give it with bg, or give pairs instead

bg.description: The background color token path, as list_tokens returns it for a color token. Give it with fg, or give pairs instead

pairs.description: Several pairs to judge in one call, each a text color token fg and a background color token bg, in place of fg and bg. At most 50

verbose.description: False leaves out the `checks` of an answer that is allowed, which shortens the answer; a denial keeps its checks, since they are the reason. Default: true

role.description: What the first color is: text (default), judged by the usage, pairs and WCAG text rules, or ui for a focus ring, border or icon stroke, judged by the usage rules and the 3:1 non-text contrast

alpha.description: Measure the first color at this opacity, 0 to 1, on top of any alpha the token already has (the two multiply). The pair still names tokens; only the measured ratio changes. Default: the token as it is

theme.description: Judge the pair in this context of the resolver's theme modifier, such as dark. Default: the default tokens

allowed.description: True when the brand allows this text color on this background; with `pairs`, true when it allows every pair

results.description: With `pairs`: one answer for each pair, in order, each with the fields of a single answer: fg, bg, allowed, reason, role, contrast and, unless `verbose` is false and the pair is allowed, checks

reason.description: The rule that decided the answer

contrast.description: The contrast ratio of the pair, the strictest WCAG level it meets, and for role ui the threshold it had to reach. Absent when a usage rule denied a pair whose colors cannot be measured

name: measure_contrast
title: Measure the contrast of a color
description: Measures the contrast of one color token on another, optionally with one translucent color token blended over the background first. It is a measurement of what would be rendered, not a verdict: the answer has no `allowed` and does not say whether the brand approves; only `can_use` says whether the brand allows a pair, and a blend is never a listed pair. Use it for a tint or glow that no token names: give the opaque base `bg`, the tinting token as `with` and its opacity as `withAlpha`. `alpha` is the foreground's own opacity and `withAlpha` is the opacity of `with` over `bg`; they are different. `with` and `withAlpha` come together or not at all. The answer is `ratio` (WCAG 2.x), `level`, `nonText` (true from 3:1), `seen` (the two colors after blending, as hex) and `brandPairs`: the pairs the brand lists for this `fg` on the BASE `bg` token, not on the blend. A gradient is not measured: pass the color of its strongest point as `with` and that point's opacity as `withAlpha`. Refused, never guessed: a translucent `bg`, a `with` that is not a color blazon can read, an unknown token, `with` without `withAlpha` or the reverse, an opacity outside 0 to 1.

fg.description: The foreground color token path, as list_tokens returns it for a color token

bg.description: The base background color token path. It must be opaque: a background with an alpha channel is refused

with.description: A color token blended over `bg`, such as a glow or tint no token names. Give it with `withAlpha`. A gradient is refused: pass its strongest point

withAlpha.description: The opacity of `with` composited over `bg`, 0 to 1, on top of any alpha the `with` token has (the two multiply). Not the foreground opacity: that is `alpha`. Give it with `with`

alpha.description: The foreground's own opacity, 0 to 1, as `can_use` takes it, on top of any alpha the token has. Not the opacity of `with`: that is `withAlpha`. Default: the token as it is

theme.description: Measure in this context of the resolver's theme modifier, such as dark. Default: the default tokens

name: get_fonts

description: Gets the font stylesheets and font files the brand loads, and for each font family a token names whether the brand loads it. Use it to load the same fonts as the brand instead of typing a font address. With css it also returns the @font-face rules for the font files, with base as their URL prefix. name: get_logo
title: Read the brand logo
description: Gets the brand logo variants for light and dark surfaces, their files, and the rules for each logo: clear space, minimum size, lockups, and the backgrounds that forbid it. Use it before placing a logo. Give `on`, a background color token, to have blazon pick the logo for it: the answer then has `pick`, the file that reads best there with its contrast, or a `refused` that says whether a `logo` deny rule, too little contrast or an unmeasurable background left none. For the brand's other rules use get_rules.

on.description: A background color token path. The answer then has `pick`: the logo to place on it

lockup.description: With `on`: only the logo assets of this lockup (horizontal, stacked, mark, wordmark, or one the brand added)
